_note: STAR FALL environmental vocabulary library (English). Typing targets are lowercase a-z single words, American spelling. Definitions and examples are original short text written for this game; see docs/vocabulary.md for review status and sources.

entries.definition: The invisible mix of gases that living things breathe.
entries.example: Trees help keep the air fresh.

entries.definition: The star that gives our planet light and heat.
entries.example: The sun warms the soil in spring.

entries.definition: A tall plant with a woody trunk and branches.
entries.example: We planted a tree beside the school.

entries.definition: The top layer of ground where plants grow.
entries.example: Healthy soil is full of tiny living things.

entries.definition: A small part of a plant that can grow into a new plant.
entries.example: She pressed a seed into the warm soil.

entries.definition: The clear liquid that fills rivers, lakes, and oceans.
entries.example: Every living thing needs clean water.

entries.definition: Free from dirt, waste, or harmful substances.
entries.example: The volunteers left the beach clean.

entries.definition: A flat green part of a plant that catches sunlight.
entries.example: A leaf turns sunlight into food for the tree.

entries.definition: Water that falls from clouds in drops.
entries.example: Rain refills the pond each spring.

entries.definition: Moving air.
entries.example: The wind turned the tall white turbine.

entries.definition: A large area of salt water.
entries.example: The sea was calm that morning.

entries.definition: A large body of water surrounded by land.
entries.example: Ducks rested on the quiet lake.

entries.definition: A small, still body of water.
entries.example: Frogs laid their eggs in the pond.

entries.definition: A large stream of water that flows across land.
entries.example: The river carried fresh water to the valley.

entries.definition: An animal with feathers and wings.
entries.example: A bird built its nest in the hedge.

entries.definition: An animal that lives and breathes in water.
entries.example: The fish swam between the rocks.

entries.definition: A flying insect that collects nectar and spreads pollen.
entries.example: A bee moved from flower to flower.
entries.note: Bees help many food plants make fruit and seeds.

entries.definition: A small animal that lives both on land and in water.
entries.example: The frog jumped back into the pond.

entries.definition: A living thing that usually grows in soil and makes its own food.
entries.example: Water the plant once a week.

entries.definition: Green plants with thin leaves that cover fields and lawns.
entries.example: Sheep grazed on the long grass.

entries.definition: The colorful part of a plant that makes seeds.
entries.example: The flower attracted a butterfly.

entries.definition: The part of a plant that grows underground and takes in water.
entries.example: A root holds the tree firmly in the ground.

entries.definition: The tough outer covering of a tree trunk.
entries.example: Bark protects a tree from insects.

entries.definition: The hard material that forms a tree's trunk and branches.
entries.example: The bench was made from reclaimed wood.

entries.definition: Soft, wet soil.
entries.example: Pigs cool off by rolling in mud.

entries.definition: A hard, solid piece of the ground.
entries.example: Moss grew on the shady side of the rock.

entries.definition: Tiny grains of rock found on beaches and in deserts.
entries.example: The tide smoothed the sand.

entries.definition: A moving ridge of water on the surface of the sea.
entries.example: A wave washed over the shells.

entries.definition: Water that has frozen solid.
entries.example: The ice on the lake melted in April.

entries.definition: Soft white flakes of frozen water that fall from clouds.
entries.example: Snow covered the hills.

entries.definition: A mass of tiny water drops floating in the sky.
entries.example: A dark cloud brought rain.

entries.definition: Things people throw away because they no longer want them.
entries.example: Put your trash in the bin, not on the path.

entries.definition: A container for holding waste or recycling.
entries.example: The blue bin is for paper.

entries.definition: A metal container for food or drink.
entries.example: An empty can is easy to recycle.

entries.definition: A soft container made of paper, cloth, or plastic.
entries.example: Bring a cloth bag to the shop.

entries.definition: A glass or plastic container with a wide opening.
entries.example: We reuse the jar to store seeds.

entries.definition: A container with flat sides, often made of cardboard.
entries.example: Fold the box before recycling it.

entries.definition: A device that gives light.
entries.example: Switch off the lamp when you leave.

entries.definition: Warmth, or the energy that makes things hot.
entries.example: Thick walls keep heat inside the house.

entries.definition: The energy that lets us see.
entries.example: Sunlight streamed through the window.

entries.definition: To look after something and keep it safe.
entries.example: We care for the garden every weekend.

entries.definition: To keep something from being wasted or lost.
entries.example: Turn off the tap to save water.

entries.definition: The planet we live on; also the ground or soil.
entries.example: Earth is the only home we have.

entries.definition: The place where a person or animal lives.
entries.example: The hollow log is home to a family of mice.

entries.definition: A shelter that birds and some animals build for their young.
entries.example: The robin laid three eggs in its nest.

entries.definition: A public area of land with grass and trees.
entries.example: The town park has a new wildflower bed.

entries.definition: Land used for growing crops or raising animals.
entries.example: The farm grows apples for the village.

entries.definition: The part of a plant that holds its seeds and can often be eaten.
entries.example: Fruit trees feed both birds and people.

entries.definition: Covered with plants, or kind to the environment.
entries.example: The city wants more green space.

entries.definition: Loose soil.
entries.example: The dog dug happily in the dirt.

entries.definition: A thick cloud close to the ground.
entries.example: Fog drifted over the marsh at dawn.

entries.definition: A raised area of land, smaller than a mountain.
entries.example: Wildflowers covered the hill.

entries.definition: To use something again instead of throwing it away.
entries.example: We reuse glass jars for paint.

entries.definition: Material that is thrown away or used carelessly.
entries.example: Food waste can become compost.

entries.definition: Trash left lying in a public place.
entries.example: The class picked up litter in the park.

entries.definition: A large area covered with trees.
entries.example: The forest is home to deer and owls.

entries.definition: To process used materials so they can be made into new things.
entries.example: We recycle paper, cans, and bottles.

entries.definition: To keep something safe from harm.
entries.example: Fences protect the young trees from deer.

entries.definition: To make something smaller in amount.
entries.example: We reduce waste by buying less packaging.

entries.definition: To fix something that is broken.
entries.example: Repair the bike instead of buying a new one.
entries.note: Repairing keeps things in use and out of the trash.

entries.definition: A light, strong material made mostly from oil.
entries.example: Some plastic lasts for hundreds of years.

entries.definition: Thin material made from wood pulp, used for writing and packing.
entries.example: Paper can be recycled several times.

entries.definition: A hard, clear material made by melting sand.
entries.example: Glass can be melted and reshaped again and again.

entries.definition: A hard material such as iron, steel, or aluminum.
entries.example: Old metal was melted down to make new tools.

entries.definition: A container with a narrow neck for holding liquids.
entries.example: Refill your water bottle at the fountain.

entries.definition: A piece of land where plants are grown.
entries.example: The school garden grows beans and peas.

entries.definition: A small animal with six legs and a body in three parts.
entries.example: An insect hotel gives beetles a place to shelter.

entries.definition: A living thing that can move and must eat to survive.
entries.example: Every animal needs food, water, and shelter.

entries.definition: One of the very large bodies of salt water on the planet.
entries.example: The ocean covers most of the planet.

entries.definition: A small, narrow river.
entries.example: Trout swim in the cold stream.

entries.definition: A place where water flows naturally out of the ground.
entries.example: The village drew water from a spring.

entries.definition: The land along the edge of a sea or lake.
entries.example: Shells were scattered along the shore.

entries.definition: A sandy or pebbly shore by the sea.
entries.example: We cleaned the beach after the storm.

entries.definition: The regular rise and fall of the sea.
entries.example: At low tide we found crabs in the rock pools.

entries.definition: A ridge of rock, sand, or coral near the surface of the sea.
entries.example: Bright fish shelter in the reef.

entries.definition: A hard structure built by tiny sea animals that forms reefs.
entries.example: Coral needs clear, warm water to grow.

entries.definition: The hard outer covering of some sea animals.
entries.example: A crab hid inside an empty shell.

entries.definition: A part of a tree that grows out from the trunk.
entries.example: A squirrel ran along the branch.

entries.definition: The main woody stem of a tree.
entries.example: The trunk was too wide to hug.

entries.definition: The top layer of leaves formed by the crowns of trees.
entries.example: Monkeys live high in the canopy.

entries.definition: A small, soft green plant that grows in damp places.
entries.example: Moss covered the fallen log.

entries.definition: A living thing, such as a mushroom, that feeds on dead or living matter.
entries.example: A fungus helps break down fallen leaves.
entries.note: Fungi return nutrients from dead wood to the soil.

entries.definition: The state of the air at a certain time and place.
entries.example: The weather turned stormy in the afternoon.

entries.definition: One of the four parts of the year.
entries.example: Each season brings changes to the forest.

entries.definition: Energy that makes machines and devices work.
entries.example: Solar panels provide power for the cabin.

entries.definition: The ability to do work, such as moving, heating, or lighting.
entries.example: Food gives our bodies energy.

entries.definition: Relating to the sun, or powered by sunlight.
entries.example: Solar panels turned sunlight into electricity.

entries.definition: A material that is burned or used up to make energy.
entries.example: Wood was once the main fuel for cooking.

entries.definition: The gray or black cloud given off by something burning.
entries.example: Smoke from the fire filled the valley.

entries.definition: A haze of smoke, fog, and other pollution that hangs in the air.
entries.example: Smog hid the mountains from view.
entries.note: Smog is a visible sign of air pollution over cities.

entries.definition: Tiny dry particles of soil or other matter.
entries.example: Dust blew off the dry fields.

entries.definition: A thick liquid from underground, used as fuel and to make plastic.
entries.example: Spilled oil coats the feathers of seabirds.

entries.definition: An accidental release of a liquid, often a harmful one.
entries.example: Crews worked for weeks to clean up the spill.

entries.definition: Poisonous and harmful to living things.
entries.example: Toxic chemicals must never be poured down the drain.

entries.definition: Damage or injury.
entries.example: Loud noise can harm wildlife.

entries.definition: To use or enjoy something together with others.
entries.example: We share the river with many animals.

entries.definition: To save someone or something from danger.
entries.example: Volunteers rescue turtles caught in nets.

entries.definition: A large body in space that moves around a star.
entries.example: Our planet is covered with oceans and forests.

entries.definition: The plants, animals, land, and other parts of the world not made by people.
entries.example: We spent the day exploring nature.

entries.definition: Living or growing naturally, without care from people.
entries.example: Wild berries grew along the trail.

entries.definition: A field of grass and wildflowers.
entries.example: Butterflies drifted across the meadow.

entries.definition: Low land between hills or mountains.
entries.example: A river ran through the valley.

entries.definition: Low, wet land often covered with tall grasses.
entries.example: Herons hunt for fish in the marsh.

entries.definition: To arrange things into groups.
entries.example: Sort the recycling into paper, glass, and cans.

entries.definition: To fill something again after it has been emptied.
entries.example: Refill the soap bottle at the shop.

entries.definition: To give something away to help others.
entries.example: We donate old clothes instead of throwing them out.
entries.note: Donating gives items a second life instead of sending them to a landfill.

entries.definition: An animal that is hunted by another animal for food.
entries.example: Mice are prey for foxes and hawks.

entries.definition: The natural home of a plant or animal.
entries.example: The wetland is a habitat for many birds.

entries.definition: Rotted plant and food waste used to enrich soil.
entries.example: Our compost turns vegetable peels into rich soil.

entries.definition: To protect something and use it carefully so it lasts.
entries.example: Short showers help conserve water.

entries.definition: To bring something back to a good condition.
entries.example: The group worked to restore the old wetland.

entries.definition: Animals and plants that live in natural conditions.
entries.example: The reserve protects local wildlife.

entries.definition: The process of turning used materials into new products.
entries.example: Recycling keeps metal out of landfills.

entries.definition: A place where waste is buried under layers of soil.
entries.example: The landfill was almost full.

entries.definition: Food scraps and other things that are thrown away.
entries.example: Garbage trucks collect waste every Tuesday.

entries.definition: The boxes, wrappers, and containers that products come in.
entries.example: Choose products with less packaging.

entries.definition: A supply of something useful, such as water, wood, or minerals.
entries.example: Fresh water is a precious resource.

entries.definition: Powered by or relating to electricity.
entries.example: The town bought electric buses.

entries.definition: A device that stores energy and supplies it as electricity.
entries.example: Old batteries need special recycling.
entries.note: Batteries contain metals that should not end up in landfills.

entries.definition: A machine with blades that turn to produce power.
entries.example: The wind turbine spun all night.

entries.definition: The usual weather of a place over many years.
entries.example: The climate in the north is cold and dry.

entries.definition: A long period with little or no rain.
entries.example: The drought dried up the farm ponds.

entries.definition: A large amount of water covering land that is usually dry.
entries.example: Wetlands can soak up water and soften a flood.

entries.definition: A huge, slow-moving mass of ice.
entries.example: The glacier has shrunk over the past century.

entries.definition: Land that is soaked with water, such as a marsh or swamp.
entries.example: A wetland filters water and shelters birds.

entries.definition: The wide part of a river where it meets the sea.
entries.example: Young fish grow up in the estuary.
entries.note: Fresh and salt water mix here, making a rich nursery for sea life.

entries.definition: A tree that grows in salty coastal water.
entries.example: Mangrove roots shelter young fish.
entries.note: Mangrove forests protect coasts from storms and erosion.

entries.definition: A fine powder made by flowers that helps plants make seeds.
entries.example: Bees carry pollen from flower to flower.

entries.definition: A sweet liquid made by flowers.
entries.example: Hummingbirds drink nectar.
entries.note: Nectar is the reward that draws pollinators to flowers.

entries.definition: A group of living things that are alike and can breed together.
entries.example: The forest holds hundreds of species of beetle.

entries.definition: An animal that hunts other animals for food.
entries.example: The owl is a night predator.
entries.note: Predators keep prey numbers in balance.

entries.definition: To move from one region to another with the seasons.
entries.example: Geese migrate south for the winter.

entries.definition: A place that gives protection from weather or danger.
entries.example: Hedges give birds shelter from the wind.

entries.definition: A young plant grown from a seed.
entries.example: Each student planted a seedling.

entries.definition: A young tree.
entries.example: The sapling needs a stake until it grows strong.

entries.definition: Land covered with trees, usually less dense than a forest.
entries.example: Bluebells carpet the woodland in spring.

entries.definition: The cutting down of trees for wood.
entries.example: Careless logging can strip a hillside bare.

entries.definition: Wood prepared for building.
entries.example: The cabin was built from local timber.

entries.definition: To make air, water, or land dirty and harmful.
entries.example: Factories must not pollute the river.

entries.definition: The waste gases released by an engine.
entries.example: Car exhaust adds to air pollution.

entries.definition: A substance made by or used in chemistry.
entries.example: Store garden chemicals away from streams.

entries.definition: Waste water and waste matter carried away in sewers.
entries.example: Treated sewage is cleaned before it reaches the river.

entries.definition: Rainwater that flows over land into streams, often carrying dirt or chemicals.
entries.example: Runoff from the fields carried fertilizer into the lake.
entries.note: Runoff is how pollution on land reaches rivers and seas.

entries.definition: The slow wearing away of soil or rock by wind or water.
entries.example: Tree roots help stop erosion on steep slopes.

entries.definition: A natural solid substance found in rocks and soil.
entries.example: Plants absorb minerals from the soil.

entries.definition: A substance that living things need to grow and stay healthy.
entries.example: Compost adds nutrients to the garden.

entries.definition: Coming from living things, or grown without artificial chemicals.
entries.example: Leaves and peels are organic waste.

entries.definition: An area of land set aside to protect plants and animals.
entries.example: The nature reserve is closed to cars.

entries.definition: To plant again, especially trees in a cleared area.
entries.example: Volunteers replant the hillside every autumn.

entries.definition: To return to a healthy state.
entries.example: The river began to recover once the dumping stopped.

entries.definition: An effort to remove litter or pollution from a place.
entries.example: The beach cleanup filled forty bags.

entries.definition: A person who offers to help without being paid.
entries.example: A volunteer showed us how to sort recycling.

entries.definition: To treat something as important and worth protecting.
entries.example: Respect wildlife by keeping your distance.

entries.definition: Able to be recycled.
entries.example: Check whether the container is recyclable.

entries.definition: Able to be used again.
entries.example: She carries a reusable cup.

entries.definition: To turn old or waste items into something of greater value.
entries.example: We upcycle old tires into planters.
entries.note: Upcycling keeps materials in use without breaking them down first.

entries.definition: To gather crops when they are ripe.
entries.example: The farmers harvest the wheat in late summer.

entries.definition: The amount of rain that falls in a place.
entries.example: Rainfall was low this year.

entries.definition: A layer of underground rock or gravel that holds water.
entries.example: The town's wells draw from an aquifer.
entries.note: Many communities depend on aquifers for drinking water.

entries.definition: A chemical element found in all living things and in fuels like coal.
entries.example: Burning coal releases carbon into the air.
entries.note: Carbon released by burning fuel warms the climate.

entries.definition: A gas or other substance released into the air.
entries.example: The new bus has a lower emission rate.

entries.definition: Something that could cause harm.
entries.example: Broken glass on the trail is a hazard.

entries.definition: Harmful substances that make air, water, or land dirty.
entries.example: Air pollution can make people sick.

entries.definition: A community of living things and their surroundings, working together.
entries.example: A pond is a small ecosystem.

entries.definition: The variety of all living things in a place.
entries.example: Rainforests have rich biodiversity.

entries.definition: The careful protection of nature and natural resources.
entries.example: Conservation keeps rare animals from disappearing.

entries.definition: Meeting present needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs.
entries.example: Sustainability means thinking about the future.

entries.definition: Able to continue for a long time without damaging the environment.
entries.example: Sustainable fishing leaves enough fish to breed.

entries.definition: Able to be replaced naturally, like sunlight or wind.
entries.example: Wind is a renewable source of energy.

entries.definition: The clearing of forests on a large scale.
entries.example: Deforestation destroys animal habitats.

entries.definition: Planting trees where a forest has been cut down.
entries.example: Reforestation brought birds back to the valley.

entries.definition: The process plants use to turn sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into food.
entries.example: Photosynthesis releases oxygen into the air.

entries.definition: The layer of gases that surrounds a planet.
entries.example: The atmosphere shields the planet from harmful rays.

entries.definition: The natural world and the conditions around living things.
entries.example: We all share responsibility for the environment.

entries.definition: The presence of something harmful that makes a substance unsafe.
entries.example: Tests found contamination in the well water.

entries.definition: To break down slowly into simpler substances.
entries.example: Leaves decompose into rich soil.

entries.definition: Able to be broken down naturally by bacteria and other living things.
entries.example: Banana peels are biodegradable.

entries.definition: A tiny piece of plastic less than five millimeters long.
entries.example: Microplastic has been found in the deep ocean.
entries.note: Microplastic forms when larger plastic waste breaks apart.

entries.definition: At risk of disappearing forever.
entries.example: The endangered frog lives in only one valley.

entries.definition: The dying out of a whole species.
entries.example: Habitat loss is a leading cause of extinction.

entries.definition: A glass building that traps the sun's heat to keep plants warm.
entries.example: Tomatoes grow well in a greenhouse.
entries.note: The greenhouse effect is named after the way these buildings trap heat.

entries.definition: Getting the most use out of energy or materials with the least waste.
entries.example: LED bulbs improve energy efficiency.

entries.definition: Using heat from deep inside the ground.
entries.example: Geothermal plants turn underground heat into electricity.

entries.definition: Producing electricity from moving water.
entries.example: The hydroelectric dam powers the city.

entries.definition: An animal, such as a bee or bat, that carries pollen between flowers.
entries.example: A garden full of flowers helps every pollinator.

entries.definition: An area of land that drains into a river, lake, or sea.
entries.example: Everything in the watershed affects the river downstream.
entries.note: What happens anywhere in a watershed reaches the water below.

entries.definition: Water held underground in soil and rock.
entries.example: Wells pump groundwater to the surface.

entries.definition: Removing salt from seawater to make it safe to drink.
entries.example: Desalination uses a lot of energy.

entries.definition: The responsible care of something entrusted to you.
entries.example: Stewardship of the forest passed to the next generation.
entries.note: Stewardship means caring for nature on behalf of others, including the future.

entries.definition: Being responsible for your actions and their results.
entries.example: Companies need accountability for the waste they create.

entries.definition: The natural regrowth of a damaged area.
entries.example: After the fire, regeneration began within a year.

entries.definition: The using up of goods, energy, or resources.
entries.example: Lower consumption means less waste.
entries.note: How much we consume decides how much waste we make.

entries.definition: The burning of waste.
entries.example: Incineration shrinks waste but can pollute the air.

entries.definition: A substance added to soil to help plants grow.
entries.example: Too much fertilizer can wash into lakes.
entries.note: Excess fertilizer feeds algae that choke rivers and lakes.

entries.definition: A chemical used to kill pests that damage crops.
entries.example: Some pesticides also harm bees.

entries.definition: Returning something to its earlier, healthier condition.
entries.example: Wetland restoration brought the herons back.

entries.definition: Keeping something safe from harm or decay.
entries.example: Preservation of old forests protects rare plants.

entries.definition: Relating to living things and their surroundings.
entries.example: The spill caused serious ecological damage.

entries.definition: Material that slows the flow of heat in or out of a building.
entries.example: Good insulation keeps a house warm with less fuel.
entries.note: Less heat lost means less energy burned.
